property_summary: For any caller and any new owner different from the current one, setOwner succeeds only when the caller is the current owner (owner becomes newOwner) and otherwise reverts leaving owner unchanged; the inverted-require mutant inverts this so an owner's call reverts while a non-owner's call succeeds, breaking the rule.
For any caller and address, a successful setOwner call returns true; the mutant returns false, breaking this rule.
For any caller equal to the current owner and any new owner address, setOwner must complete and return true; the mutant returns false for the same calls.
p_diagnostic: testFuzz_property(address,address): `vm.assume` rejected too many inputs (65536 allowed)

property_summary: For any caller equal to the current owner and any new address, a successful setOwner call must set the owner to that address and return exactly true; the mutant never changes the owner and returns owner != _owner, which is false when _owner equals the current owner (or when the new owner equals the old one).

For any caller equal to the current owner and any proposed address (including the current owner itself), a successful setOwner call must return exactly true; the mutant returns (owner != _owner), which is false whenever _owner equals the current owner.
For any address newOwner, calling setOwner(newOwner) as the current owner sets c.owner() to exactly newOwner; the mutant instead sets it to msg.sender, so any newOwner != msg.sender breaks the rule.

For every candidate address, calling setOwner as the current owner must set c.owner() to exactly that address; the buggy version instead sets owner to the zero address, breaking this for any nonzero candidate.

For any caller equal to the current owner and any address newOwner, a successful setOwner(newOwner) leaves c.owner() equal to newOwner; the mutant overwrites it to address(0), breaking this for any newOwner != address(0).
